name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
title: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
answer: This page covers data loss prevention and sanitisation for artificial intelligence systems in enterprise settings. It addresses how sensitive information can enter training data, prompts, model outputs, logs, and retrieval sources, and how organisations can block or remove that information before it is stored, shared, or used to train a model. The focus is on audit readiness and safe enablement of AI tools, including generative models and retrieval augmented generation.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: DLP controls for AI typically sit at the network edge, API gateway, model serving layer, and data pipeline. Sanitisation runs in preprocessing steps for training and fine-tuning data, in prompt filtering before a request reaches a model, and in output filtering before a response is returned to a user. Logging and monitoring systems also need DLP rules because prompts and outputs are often retained for audit or debugging.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work combines pattern matching for known identifiers such as credit card numbers or personal names, named entity recognition for less structured text, and context based classifiers that flag confidential business material. Sanitisation methods include redaction, tokenisation, pseudonymisation, and data minimisation, where only the fields needed for a task are sent to a model. Output filters then check generated text for residual sensitive content before it leaves the system.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk centre on confidentiality, data protection obligations, intellectual property leakage, and contractual limits on how third party models may use enterprise data. Provenance matters because a sanitised dataset or prompt log must show what was removed, when, and under which policy, so that auditors can verify compliance. Incident response for AI data loss follows the same breach notification duties as other systems, but the risk surface includes model memory and cached outputs.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: DLP and sanitisation are moving toward real time, context aware filtering that can follow a document through retrieval, generation, and agent tool use. Privacy preserving techniques such as differential privacy and on device redaction are becoming more practical for enterprise AI. Regulatory pressure and audit requirements will push organisations to keep machine readable provenance records for every sanitisation decision, and model unlearning may become a standard control for removing sensitive data after the fact.
